headlines.summary: Any button that can be clicked can also be touched.
headlines.article_text: Hands-on with Apple's first touchscreen laptop Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points Apple announced its first touchscreen laptop models on Wednesday at an event in Los Angeles. Here's the good news for anyone who is worried about the new user interface: You don't have to use it. Apple said it used an oleophobic coating on its screens to resist fingerprints. It appears to work. In this article AAPL Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT watch now VIDEO 1:59 01:59 Apple's new touchscreen Macbook Pro — first impressions News Videos Apple announced its first touchscreen laptop models on Wednesday at an event in Los Angeles. These new MacBooks, called MacBook Pro with ProLED XDR Display, are still Apple MacBooks. They run MacOS, not iPadOS or iOS, the iPhone's operating system. Here's the good news for anyone who is worried about the new user interface: You don't have to use it. Touch is entirely optional. CNBC briefly tested both the 14-inch and 16-inch touchscreen MacBooks at the event. Users can still primarily or entirely use the device's trackpad and keyboard, and there are few visual updates. MacOS still looks largely the same as it used to. Apple's touchscreen MacBook Pro with ProLED XDR Display. Andrew Evers | CNBC There have been a few user interface updates. For example, the red button on the top left of a window expands when you touch it to make it easier to click. Apple says that third-party developers like Microsoft and Adobe can and will update their apps to expand buttons and other touch targets to be larger. I think that touch will be particularly useful to scroll through websites or documents while lying down. But even software that hasn't been explicitly updated for the new computer will support touch. Apple says that behind the scenes, its software converts every touch tap into a traditional click. So any button that can be clicked can also be touched. Using the laptop with your finger feels good, but it won't change the way most people use their laptops. It could be useful for iPhone app developers, who can now test the way their apps work on their Mac. An accessibility feature allows users to pinch to zoom on any part of the user interface. Apple said on Wednesday that it had used an oleophobic coating on its screens to resist fingerprints. It appears to work. I didn't notice marks on the screen when I used the touch features. Apple is also, in addition to the touch feature, marketing these laptops as having a superior display, thanks to its new tandem OLED technology that offers deeper blacks and higher contrast. While photos and other art looked great on the screen, it's not a night-and-day difference from past Apple laptops. A lot of the improvements are aimed at creators who need accurate colors for photo and video editing. Apple's touchscreen MacBook Pro with ProLED XDR Display and 12MP Center Stage camera. Andrew Evers | CNBC Instead of the notch at the top of previous MacBooks, where Apple hides its cameras, the new MacBooks have a hole-punch cutout in the display, like recent iPhones. Apple's Dynamic Island feature — new to the MacBook — expands to show live activities and Siri. Apple made a big deal about the laptop's new hinge, which is meant to keep the screen from shaking when you touch it. For example, if you tap the screen on a video call, your camera won't shake as much. But the hinge feels largely the same as Apple's previous MacBook Pros. There is one new feature that is immediately noticeable and tells people you bought the latest, greatest, and most expensive Apple laptop. (The smaller 14-inch model starts at $2,899 and the bigger one costs at least $3,399.) The Apple logo on the lid now lights up when the computer is on. It's the first Apple laptop that supports it since the 2017 MacBook Air. Apple’s new touchscreen MacBook Pro. Andrew Evers | CNBC The light-up logo drew a cheer from analysts and influencers in attendance when it was announced on Wednesday. headlines.article_text: Microsoft (MSFT) Q1 earnings report 2027 Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points Microsoft reported 19% revenue growth, topping estimates. Azure cloud revenue jumped 48% to $33.2 billion. Free cash flow declined 27% from a year ago. In this article MSFT Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella speaks at a company event at La Defense business district in Puteaux, near Paris, on Oct. 20, 2026. Dimitar Dilkoff | AFP | Getty Images Microsoft shares rose 4% in extended trading on Wednesday after the company reported better-than-expected quarterly results, driven by 48% growth in its Azure cloud infrastructure business. Here's how the company fared relative to LSEG consensus: Earnings per share: $4.89 adjusted vs. $4.73 expected Revenue: $92.28 billion vs. $90.69 billion expected Microsoft's revenue grew 19% year over year in the quarter, which ended on Sept. 30, according to a statement , with Azure now its biggest single business. The software giant has been rapidly building out data center infrastructure to meet artificial intelligence demand, while also maintaining positive free cash flow unlike its fellow hyperscalers. Microsoft reported $45.2 billion worth of capital expenditures and finance leases during the quarter, up about 30% from a year earlier. Analysts surveyed by StreetAccount had projected $50.67 billion. With respect to guidance, Microsoft called for $96 billion to $97.1 billion in fiscal second-quarter revenue, which works out to 18.8% growth at the middle of the range. Analysts polled by LSEG had predicted $95.60 billion in revenue. For Azure, Hood said she anticipates 49% to 50% growth at constant currency for the fiscal second quarter, compared with the 45.1% StreetAccount consensus. "We still have demand that exceeds supply," she said. During the fiscal first quarter, Microsoft flagged a higher growth rate for cash paid for property and equipment than overall capital expenditures, which include finance leases. "Some third-party capacity deliveries we expected in Q1 were delayed," the company's finance chief, Amy Hood, said on a conference call with analysts. Around 75% of capital expenditures are now tied to short-lived assets such as Intel chips and Nvidia graphics processing units, up from about 66% in the past three quarters and half in the year-ago quarter. The shift indicates Microsoft's prioritization of infrastructure it can can quickly turn into revenue. Hood said the company is aiming at over $50 billion in fiscal second-quarter capital expenditures and finance leases, above the StreetAccount consensus of $53.10 billion, with $170 billion for all of calendar 2027 because of the capacity issues. "In the second half of the fiscal year, we currently expect capex spend to accelerate primarily from CPUs, inclusive of higher memory and storage costs, and GPUs, as well as the 3P capacity deliveries that shifted to H2," she said. The delays have to do with GPU-as-a-service providers, she said. Free cash flow for the fiscal first quarter declined 27% to $18.63 billion. headlines.article_text: MacBook Pro: Apple brings touch to the Mac Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points Apple announced its first laptop with a touchscreen will go on sale Nov. 6. The launch signifies the growing strategic importance of the Mac to Apple, despite it generating less revenue than the iPhone. Global PC shipments have fallen and Apple faces pressure from rising memory costs and higher computer prices. Touchscreens have not typically driven laptop purchases, making Apple's software changes and developer strategy central to whether the feature catches on. In this article AAPL Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT watch now VIDEO 1:59 01:59 Apple's new touchscreen Macbook Pro — first impressions News Videos Apple on Wednesday announced its first laptop with a touchscreen, which it's calling MacBook Pro with ProLED XDR Display. Apple said the laptop has a new display, using OLED technology, that offers more brightness, better colors and wider viewing angles. It's using Apple's M5 Pro or Max chips, and Apple said Wednesday that it's lighter than Apple's current Pro laptops. It's still an Apple laptop, and is running MacOS, not a version of the iPhone or iPad operating system. In a video, Apple showed users swiping on the screen to manipulate videos or images. It also has a glowing Apple logo on the laptop's lid. The new laptop will go on sale Nov. 6 and the 14-inch version will start at $2,899. The 16-inch version will cost at least $3,399. Both are notable price increases from existing models. This is Apple's third major product launch under new CEO John Ternus, signaling a faster cadence for hardware releases. It's also a major reversal for Apple, which has resisted putting touchscreens on its laptops for decades as some Windows machines gained the feature. German-Russian record producer and DJ Zedd, at left, and Apple CEO John Ternus look at the new M6 14-inch MacBook Pro during the Apple Experience LA event in Los Angeles, Oct. 28, 2026. Frederic J. Brown | Afp | Getty Images "Yes, for the very first time, we are bringing touch to the Mac," Ternus said in live remarks to media and analysts in Los Angeles. The laptop market has been going through one of its worst slumps ever. Overall shipments are expected to be down 11% this year. Analysts say the AI-driven global market shortage of memory has contributed to higher laptop prices, which has hurt sales and demand. In the third quarter, total PC shipments dropped 20% on a year-over-year basis, according to market researcher IDC. Apple's own shipments fell 11% during the quarter, according to the estimate. Even Apple's not immune to rising memory prices, after then-CEO Tim Cook warned this summer that the situation around memory prices was "unsustainable." Nearly all Macs got price hikes this year. Mac Minis introduced in August got a $300 bump, for example. The announcement caps a busy two months of product launches under Ternus. Apple also introduced new iMac and MacBook Pro models with M6 chips this week, after price hikes to the lineup totaling several hundred dollars in June. Apple introduced an iPad Mini on Monday that starts at $699, $100 more than its predecessor. Attendees try out the new touchscreen MacBook Pro during the Apple Experience LA in Los Angeles, Oct. 28, 2026. Frederic J. Brown | AFP | Getty Images In September, Apple released new iPhones, including its first foldable phone, the iPhone Duo. It also revealed a new smart speaker with a display called HomeView that uses a redesigned version of Siri to answer a broader range of questions. The launch signifies the growing strategic importance of the Mac to Apple, despite it generating less revenue than the iPhone. In the most recent quarter, Apple reported $10.35 billion in Mac sales, or just under 10% of the company's total revenue. But many software developers swear by the Mac, and it remains the only supported platform to develop iPhone apps. And in recent months, Apple has highlighted its chips and memory architecture to make the case that its computers are the best fit for local or edge AI that runs on a device, instead of the cloud. Meta's AI model developer team bought hundreds of Mac Minis this year to test agents, for example. And Apple notably teamed up with Meta earlier this month to make an announcement that large, nearly frontier models can run on clusters of Macs connected with high-speed cabling, allowing developers to run agentic code without paying Anthropic or OpenAI. Read more CNBC tech news Amazon’s anti-tokenmaxxing memo says engineers should be pickier about using AI Chart: Anthropic’s cash pile towers over nearly every U.S. company Google alters its cloud playbook, enlisting partners to sell more AI chips A guide to some of the biggest risks in Anthropic's IPO prospectus Apple has had a historical resistance to touchscreen laptops. Software chief Craig Federighi said in 2018 that the ergonomics would fatigue users. "We make the world's best touch computer on an iPad," Ternus, then Apple's senior VP of hardware engineering, told The Wall Street Journal in 2021. "It's totally optimized for that. And the Mac is totally optimized for indirect input. We haven't really felt a reason to change that." Ternus has been working on Macs since he joined the company and was credited along with silicon chief Johny Srouji as the leader of Apple's effort to get Macs running on Apple's chips, not Intel's. Apple credited Ternus' work on Mac in its official CEO transition statement . That may be why Ternus in his early days as CEO will be the executive to backtrack on a long-running Apple design philosophy. Touchscreen laptops have been available on Windows machines for a long time, but they're just another feature, not a selling point behind most purchasing decisions, said Ryan Reith, IDC's vice president for worldwide device trackers. Only 17% of notebook PCs shipped globally this year will have touchscreens, according to IDC data. Touchscreen laptops also have a slightly lower average selling price than non-touchscreen notebooks. Hardware technology hasn't been the limiting factor for Apple merging its desktop and mobile interfaces, he added, and Apple could have been waiting to launch a touchscreen laptop until it could present a good user experience and perfect its software after attempts to make its iPad more like a laptop. "This is really a user interface and software thing," Reith said. The service has also faced increasingly stiff competition from companies like Amazon and Walmart . After slowing its brick-and-mortar grocery effort, Amazon has doubled down on its online grocery business and leveraged its vast fulfillment footprint to speed up deliveries of household essentials, pantry staples and perishables. Both Amazon and Walmart have pushed further into same- and next-day delivery, which poses a threat to Instacart's on-demand delivery model. Analysts have noted that a potential combination of Instacart and DoorDash could attract antitrust scrutiny given the companies' market overlap. In this article F Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT watch now VIDEO 1:55 01:55 Ford reports mixed third-quarter results, says 2027 earnings will be in line with this year Today's Videos DETROIT — Ford Motor expects earnings next year will be roughly in line with the automaker's anticipated results this year, the company said Wednesday as it reported mixed results for the third quarter. The Detroit automaker beat Wall Street's third-quarter earnings expectations but slightly missed revenue estimates. The company has been working to stabilize production of its F-Series pickup trucks after dealing with supplier issues for much of the past year. "This quarter's results reflect deliberate actions to improve profitability and deliver consistent financial returns," Ford CFO Sherry House told reporters during a call Wednesday. Ford reported third-quarter adjusted free cash flow of $4.7 billion, roughly $2 billion higher than what analysts were anticipating, according to StreetAccount. Here's how Ford performed in the third quarter, compared with average estimates compiled by LSEG: Earnings per share: 49 cents adjusted vs. 40 cents expected Automotive revenue: $46.08 billion vs. $46.24 billion expected The Detroit automaker also narrowed its 2026 guidance to adjusted earnings before interest and taxes of between $10.5 billion and $11 billion, compared with a previous outlook of $10 billion to $11 billion. Ford maintained its adjusted free cash flow guidance for this year of between $6 billion and $7 billion. House said the company expects 2027 earnings to be roughly in line with this year's results, citing several offsetting factors in production issues this year as well as rising commodity costs. House noted a $1.3 billion tariff refund during the first quarter of this year was largely offset by additional costs from alternative aluminum sourcing that the company does not expect to have next year, leveling out the year-over-year comparison. She also said production of its F-Series Super Duty trucks in Canada in 2027 will make up for lost production it's expecting at its F-150 factories to retool for new models. "Next year will be the third year on our journey of increasing and improving our warranty and material cost savings, and that's getting extended to structural costs throughout the company as well in terms of savings," House said. headlines.summary: Here are some of the companies making headlines in extended trading.
headlines.article_text: Stocks making the biggest moves after hours: GOOGL, MSFT, CMG, NOW Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Here are some of the companies making headlines in extended trading. Maplebear — The company that owns Instacart gained 3% after sources familiar with the matter told CNBC that DoorDash's deal to buy the delivery service could arrive as soon as Thursday morning. DoorDash fell about 1%. Chipotle Mexican Grill — Shares gained more than 5% after the burrito chain reported same-store sales that beat estimates. Same-store sales in the third quarter grew 2.1%, versus the 1.5% increase analysts polled by FactSet anticipated. ServiceNow — The enterprise software company tumbled 15%. Third-quarter adjusted profit of $1 per share missed the LSEG consensus expectation of $1.02 a share Subscription revenue guidance for the fourth quarter ranged from $4.245 billion to $4.255 billion, while the FactSet consensus called for $4.25 billion. Fortinet — The cybersecurity company plummeted 25%. Non-GAAP gross margin for the third quarter came in at 79.6%, while analysts polled by LSEG sought 80.1%. Separately, top- and bottom-line results beat the Street's expectations. Microsoft – The software giant rose 2% after the company reported a beat on the top and bottom lines for its fiscal first-quarter earnings. Revenue came in at $92.28 billion, ahead of the $90.69 billion expected by LSEG. Meanwhile, adjusted earnings of $4.89 per share was better than the $4.73 expected by analysts. Revenue in the mega-cap's key Azure cloud business grew 48% year over year. Alphabet – Shares of the Google parent are down 9% in extended trading Wednesday after its third-quarter earnings showed the company posted negative free cash flow of $9.07 billion. Its core search revenue of $63.35 billion, missed the $64.96 billion estimate from analysts. Total company revenue of $127.58 billion also missed LSEG expectations of $128.22 billion. Align Technology — The maker of orthodontics and aesthetic dentistry products dropped 1% after fourth-quarter revenue guidance missed analysts' consensus estimates, according to FactSet data. The company also named Procter & Gamble alumna Jennifer Davis as its new CEO, effective Dec. 31. Sprouts Farmers Market — The Phoenix-based grocery chain plunged 18% after third-quarter earnings per share, revenue and same-store sales all trailed analysts' consensus estimates, according to FactSet data. Ford Motor — Shares fell nearly 2% after hours. The company reported third-quarter earnings that beat Wall Street's estimates but slightly missed on revenue. Adjusted earnings of 49 cents a share topped the LSEG consensus estimate of 40 cents per share, while revenue of $46.08 billion narrowly missed the $46.24 billion expected. FedEx — Shares fell almost 2% even as the delivery giant reported third quarter adjusted earnings that beat expectations. FedEx also said expects its full-year revenue growth at 12% year over year, up from the earlier call for an increase of roughly 11%, supported by stronger pricing and improved shipment volumes. Honeywell Aerospace — The aerospace company was down more than 2% even after raising its full-year outlook for pro forma standalone adjusted earnings per share, calling for $7.85 to $8. The company also announced an initial quarterly cash dividend of 40 cents per share. Carvana — The used car dealer climbed 10%. Carvana third-quarter revenue and adjusted EBITDA topped the numbers Wall Street had been expecting, and it said the Securities and Exchange Commission closed a previously disclosed investigation and would not take any enforcement action. CNBC's Paulina Likos, Scott Schnipper, Deena Zaidi and Nick Wells contributed reporting.
